product.olivetti-m44.summary: The Linea 1 minicomputer that expanded the M40 to combine business management and office work.
product.olivetti-m44.history: In June 1985, L’Unità presented the M44 as an addition to Olivetti’s Linea 1, intended to combine business applications and office automation under MOS. The service manual describes it as a compatible development of the M40: it retained the cabinet and supported external storage cabinets, while the M34 used a desktop enclosure. The same manual documents a later upgrade to M44SP by replacing the central unit. Sources: L’Unità, 13 June 1985, p. 10; M34/M44/M54 manual, pp. 1-1 and 1-3.
product.olivetti-m44.warning: Historical sheet under research: technical documentation preserved, without verified local firmware or an M44 platform in BluMach.
product.olivetti-m44.technical.dates: Published dates disagree. Wikipedia lists 1983; MAME records 1986 and a ROM dated March of that year. The news item of 13 June 1985 and the 1985 manual establish that the M44 already existed then, but do not fix an exact launch day.
product.olivetti-m44.technical.cpu: The new central unit accelerated the system while retaining the L1 architecture. The manual, p. 4-2, identifies UC048/A, an 8 MHz Z8001B, Z8010B MMU, MC6850 ACIA and 8253 timer. MAME’s 32 MHz annotation describes the crystal, not the CPU clock specified by Olivetti.
product.olivetti-m44.technical.memory: Memory cards allowed the system to expand. The manual, p. 1-8, supports the 512 KB RA57/E and 1, 1.5 and 2 MB RA57/C-B-A; the 1985 news item advertises up to 4 MB. The 512 KB in MAME’s comment does not by itself represent the commercial maximum.
product.olivetti-m44.technical.expansion: The cabinet housed both the CPU and its controllers. The manual, pp. 1-3/1-4, describes 14 OLIBUS positions: CPU first and initial memory second, with no gaps between boards. These are not 14 free expansion slots.
product.olivetti-m44.technical.storage: Storage choices had combination restrictions. The manual, p. 5-2, allows up to three internal peripherals, at least one removable; it offers 5.25- or 8-inch floppy drives but prohibits mixing the two sizes. External S83 and S82 cabinets extend disk and tape options.
product.olivetti-m44.technical.firmware: Booting requires M44-specific ROMs. MAME identifies pd30.128.c06 and pd29.128.a06, each 16 KiB, byte-interleaved and labelled “14 MAR. 86 REL B.1”; PL46 is listed as undumped. These are external project metadata: the bytes are not verified in the library.
product.olivetti-m44.technical.media: Preserved disk material does not yet establish bootability. The local archive contains six SCP captures and two IMG files. Container integrity was checked in September 2026; VCFed reports HxC errors for the SCP files. That external test has not been reproduced here.
product.olivetti-m44.technical.verified: The manufacturer manual, contemporary news item and MAME source have been cross-checked. BluMach has no M44 platform. MAME fc81fbe1 marks it as not working and provisionally reuses the M20 configuration, despite noting that different hardware is required.
product.olivetti-m44.technical.limitatio: The sheet cannot create or boot an M44. Firmware with provenance, PL46 characterization and verification of the memory map, controllers and reset paths are missing. The media have not been booted. A machine image with clear publication rights remains pending.
product.olivetti-m44.technical.source_ma: Olivetti, L1 M34/M44/M54 Service Manual, 188-page copy preserved from Olivrea: pp. 1-1, 1-3/1-4, 1-8, 4-2 and 5-2. It includes sheets with different document codes and June and July 1985 prefaces; it is not presented as a uniform edition.
product.olivetti-m44.technical.source_ne: L’Unità, 13 June 1985, p. 10, “Due nuovi microcomputer Olivetti”, section edited by Rossella Funghi: M44 positioning, MOS and up to 4 MB. Original page visually checked.
product.olivetti-m44.technical.source_li: Wikipedia, “Olivetti computers”, model table: 1983 attribution, preserved as a consultation extract. Cited to expose the discrepancy, not as launch evidence.
product.olivetti-m44.technical.source_ma: MAME fc81fbe1, src/mame/olivetti/m20.cpp: components, ROMs, undumped PL46, 1986 date and provisional non-working model. It does not establish physical compatibility with the M20.
product.olivetti-m44.technical.source_fo: VCFed, “Olivetti M40 / M44 L1 boot disk”: archive publication by Xolod and ldkraemer’s warning about SCP files. M40 emulator progress cited in the thread does not validate the M44.
